security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG translates `fence.hpd` as a no-op without evaluating the architecturally mandated exception conditions: at VS/VU privilege level when `hstatus.VTSR` is 1 (must raise virtual instruction exception), or at S/HS privilege level when `mstatus.TSR` is 1 (must raise illegal instruction exception). The trap gate is silently bypassed.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: fence.hpd translated without hstatus.VTSR or mstatus.TSR check; fence.hpd exception-gating not implemented in translate.c or op_helper.c; HPD fence treated as unconditional no-op; missing virtual-instruction or illegal-instruction exception for fence.hpd under TSR/VTSR=1
security_spec.summary: fence.hpd exception-gating via hstatus.VTSR (VS-level) and mstatus.TSR (S/HS-level) must be enforced in TCG translation, otherwise guest hypervisors and M-mode firmware lose the ability to trap and emulate the fence for nested/hierarchical protection domains

findings.finding: No fence.hpd instruction encoding exists in the decode tables. The generic 'fence' decode (pred:4 succ:4 wildcards) would capture any fence.hpd encoding as a regular FENCE, bypassing any HPD-specific trap gates. Zihpd/Zifencehpd extensions are not implemented.

trans_fence treats all FENCE variants as a generic full memory barrier with no TSR/VTSR exception-gating. No HPD-specific translate function exists. The Zihpd/Zifencehpd extensions are not implemented.
No ext_zifencehpd or ext_zihpd ISA extension property is registered. The closest analogue is ext_zifencei (line 137, 1246). Without an extension flag, guests cannot discover or enable HPD support.
